{{Short description|Hungarian mathematician (born 1946)}}
'''János Körner''' is a Hungarian mathematician who works on [[information theory]] and [[combinatorics]].<ref name="IEEE">{{cite web|title=Biography from IEEE|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37329125800}}</ref>

Körner studied Mathematics at the [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in Budapest with a degree in 1970<ref name=ITSOC/> and was then at the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics]] of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] until 1992.  From 1981 to 1983 he was at the [[Bell Labs|Bell Laboratories]] and in 1987–88 at [[Télécom Paris]] (ENST) in Paris.<ref name=ITSOC/> He has been a professor at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]] since 1993.<ref name="IEEE"/>

Over his career, he frequently collaborated with fellow information theorists such as [[Rudolf Ahlswede]], [[Katalin Marton]], and [[Imre Csiszár]]. Together with Rudolf Ahlswede and Peter Gács he proved the blowing-up lemma.<ref>Ahlswede, Gacs, Körner ''Bounds on conditional probabilities with applications in multiuser communication'', Z. Wahrsch. und Verw. Gebiete 34, 1976, 157–177</ref> Besides information theory, he also works on [[extremal graph theory]].

In 2014 he received the [[Claude E. Shannon Award]].<ref name=ITSOC>{{Cite web |title=János Körner |url=https://www.itsoc.org/profiles/jkorner |access-date=2020-06-12 |website=Information Theory Society}}</ref> He served as Associated editor of the [[IEEE Transactions on Information Theory]] on multiple occasions. He is a member of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.<ref name="IEEE"/>

== Books ==
* With Imre Csiszár: Information Theory: Coding Theorems for Discrete Memoryless Systems, Academic Press 1981, 2nd edition Cambridge University Press 2011.
